question: Explain how a lessee recognises and measures a lease under Ind AS 116, including the recognition exemptions available.
sources: Ind AS 116 Leases - recognition, measurement and recognition exemptions for lessees

points.label: Single on-balance-sheet model
points.description: At the commencement date the lessee recognises a right-of-use asset and a lease liability for all leases, with no operating/finance split for lessees.

points.label: Initial measurement of lease liability
points.description: The present value of lease payments not yet paid, discounted at the interest rate implicit in the lease if readily determinable, otherwise the lessee's incremental borrowing rate.
points.basis: Ind AS 116, initial measurement of the lease liability

points.label: Initial measurement of right-of-use asset
points.description: Cost: the initial lease liability plus payments made at or before commencement less incentives received, plus initial direct costs and the estimated cost of dismantling or restoring the asset.
points.basis: Ind AS 116, initial measurement of the right-of-use asset

points.label: Subsequent measurement
points.description: The asset is usually depreciated and tested for impairment; the liability is increased by interest and reduced by payments, and is remeasured when lease payments or the lease term are reassessed or the lease is modified.
points.basis: Ind AS 116, subsequent measurement by a lessee

points.label: Recognition exemptions
points.description: A lessee may choose not to apply these rules to short-term leases (12 months or less with no purchase option) and leases of low-value assets, and instead expense the payments on a straight-line or other systematic basis.
